title: (boolean), (integer), (double) and (binary) casts are deprecated
summary: PHP 8.5 deprecates the non-canonical cast names (boolean), (integer), (double) and (binary) in favor of (bool), (int), (float) and (string); each pair is a pure spelling alias with identical runtime semantics, so the rewrite is purely mechanical.
new_code_policy: Never write (boolean), (integer), (double) or (binary) in new code, in any letter casing; always use the canonical (bool), (int), (float) and (string) cast spellings.
existing_code_policy: Rewrite every (boolean)/(integer)/(double)/(binary) cast found in existing code - including any differently-cased spelling such as (Boolean) or (INTEGER) - to its canonical replacement ((bool)/(int)/(float)/(string) respectively). Unlike most deprecation cleanups, this one is safe to apply mechanically and in bulk across a whole codebase: each of the four pairs is a pure alias with identical runtime behavior, so there is no case-by-case judgment call to make and no need to inspect surrounding code before rewriting. Do not treat a (real) cast as part of this rule: (real) was already removed outright - not merely deprecated - in PHP 8.0, two minors before this catalogue's known range (8.2-8.5) begins, so code still containing it is already fatal on every version this catalogue tracks and needs a different fix (a plain (float) cast) that this rule does not cover.
guideline: Use the canonical (bool), (int), (float) and (string) cast spellings; never emit (boolean), (integer), (double) or (binary), nor any other letter-casing of them, since PHP matches cast keywords case-insensitively.
details: PHP 8.5 deprecates four non-canonical cast-name spellings. The official UPGRADING text states it in one line: "Non-canonical cast names (boolean), (integer), (double), and (binary) have been deprecated, use (bool), (int), (float), and (string) respectively." Each deprecated name maps to exactly one canonical replacement - (boolean) to (bool), (integer) to (int), (double) to (float), (binary) to (string) - and every one of the four has always been a pure alias: the deprecated and canonical spellings compile to the identical cast operation with identical runtime semantics, so swapping the keyword changes nothing about the resulting value, only which E_DEPRECATED diagnostic PHP does or does not emit starting on 8.5. PHP's cast keywords, like its other keywords, are matched case-insensitively by the parser, so (Boolean), (INTEGER), (Double), (Binary) and any other letter-casing of these four names are exactly as deprecated as the lowercase spellings the UPGRADING text uses. This deprecation has nothing to do with the (real) cast: (real) was already removed outright - not merely deprecated - in PHP 8.0, two minors before this catalogue's known range (8.2-8.5) begins, so it has no place in this rule's four-name list and no canonical replacement recorded here; a codebase that still contains (real) is already fatal on every PHP version this catalogue tracks and needs its own, different fix. As of PHP 8.5 none of (boolean)/(integer)/(double)/(binary) has been removed, only deprecated, so removed_in stays null on this rule; each of the four remains fully valid, non-deprecated syntax on every other known minor (8.2-8.4), and only code actually running on the PHP 8.5 engine sees the new diagnostic.
notes: The (real) cast is a separate, earlier matter: it was removed outright in PHP 8.0, before this catalogue's known range (8.2-8.5) begins, so it is out of scope for this rule and has no canonical-replacement mapping recorded here.

Cast keywords are matched case-insensitively, so (Boolean), (INTEGER), (Double) and (Binary) - and any other letter-casing - trigger the identical deprecation as the lowercase spellings the official text uses; a text search for this rule's four names should be case-insensitive to find every occurrence.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.5.0.txt, '4. Deprecated Functionality' -> Core: "Non-canonical cast names (boolean), (integer), (double), and (binary) have been deprecated, use (bool), (int), (float), and (string) respectively."
